title: Deuteronomy Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Deuteronomy chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Deuteronomy Chapter 6.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 6:1, what did the LORD your God command you to do with the commandments, statutes, and judgments?
options: To teach them so you might do them in the land
To write them on scrolls for others to read
To memorize and recite them daily
To hide them in your heart and never speak of them
questions.correctAnswer: To teach them so you might do them in the land
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:1 states that the LORD commanded to teach the commandments, statutes, and judgments so that you might do them in the land you go to possess.

questions.question: What reason does Deuteronomy 6:2 give for fearing the LORD your God?
options: To keep all his statutes and commandments
To avoid all trouble and hardship
To be praised by other nations
questions.correctAnswer: To keep all his statutes and commandments
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:2 explains that fearing the LORD is so you may keep all his statutes and commandments.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 6:3 says that observing the commandments will cause Israel to increase mightily in the land.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:3 states that observing the commandments will cause it to be well with Israel and that they may increase mightily in the land.

questions.question: In Deuteronomy 6:4, how is the LORD described?
options: The LORD our God is one LORD
The LORD is a mighty warrior
The LORD is merciful and slow to anger
The LORD is a jealous God
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD our God is one LORD
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:4 clearly states, 'The LORD our God is one LORD.'

questions.question: Which of the following commands is given in Deuteronomy 6:5?
options: Love the LORD thy God with all thy heart, soul, and might
Offer sacrifices at the altar daily
questions.correctAnswer: Love the LORD thy God with all thy heart, soul, and might
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:5 commands to love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, soul, and might.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 6:6, where should the words commanded this day be kept?
questions.correctAnswer: In thine heart
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:6 says, 'these words... shall be in thine heart.'

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 6:7 instructs to teach the commandments only at the temple.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:7 instructs to teach the commandments diligently to children and talk of them at home, walking, lying down, and rising up, not only at the temple.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 6:8 say about binding the words of the commandments?
options: Bind them for a sign upon thine hand and as frontlets between thine eyes
Write them on a scroll and carry it
questions.correctAnswer: Bind them for a sign upon thine hand and as frontlets between thine eyes
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:8 commands to bind the words for a sign upon the hand and as frontlets between the eyes.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 6:9, where else should the words be written?
options: Upon the posts of your house and on your gates
On the walls of the temple only
questions.correctAnswer: Upon the posts of your house and on your gates
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:9 says to write the words on the posts of thy house and on thy gates.

questions.question: Which of the following is the first instruction mentioned in Deuteronomy 6:7 for teaching children?
options: Teach them diligently unto thy children
questions.correctAnswer: Teach them diligently unto thy children
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:7 begins with the instruction to teach diligently unto thy children.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 6:4 emphasizes the unity of God as 'one LORD.'
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:4 states, 'The LORD our God is one LORD,' emphasizing the unity of God.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 6:2 says that the commandments are only for you and not for your descendants.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:2 includes you, your son, and your son's son all the days of your life, showing the commandments apply to descendants.

questions.question: In Deuteronomy 6, which instruction comes before the others listed here?
options: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD
Thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart
Teach the commandments diligently to your children
Bind the words for a sign upon thine hand
questions.correctAnswer: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:4 states 'Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD,' which comes before the other instructions listed in verses 5, 7, and 8.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 6:1 say you will do in the land whither ye go?
options: Do the commandments, statutes, and judgments
questions.correctAnswer: Do the commandments, statutes, and judgments
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:1 says that the commandments, statutes, and judgments are commanded to teach you so that ye might do them in the land.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 6:3, what is promised if Israel observes to do the commandments?
options: It may be well with thee and ye may increase mightily
Ye shall become kings over other nations
Ye shall never face any enemies
questions.correctAnswer: It may be well with thee and ye may increase mightily
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:3 promises that if Israel observes the commandments, it will be well with them and they may increase mightily.

medium.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Deuteronomy Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will the LORD give you when He brings you into the land He swore to your fathers according to Deuteronomy 6:10?
options: Great and goodly cities which you built not
questions.correctAnswer: Great and goodly cities which you built not
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:10 states that the LORD will bring you into a land with great and goodly cities which you did not build. This is further confirmed by verse 11 mentioning houses full of all good things which you did not fill.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 6:11, what are some things in the land that you did not create or plant?
questions.correctAnswer: Wells, vineyards, and olive trees
questions.explanation: Verse 11 lists wells dug, vineyards, and olive trees that you did not dig or plant, emphasizing God’s provision for the people in the promised land.

questions.question: What warning does Deuteronomy 6:12 give about the blessings received in the promised land?
options: Beware lest thou forget the LORD who brought you out of Egypt
Forget the LORD and worship other gods
Build altars to gods of the surrounding nations
Ignore the commandments of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Beware lest thou forget the LORD who brought you out of Egypt
questions.explanation: Verse 12 warns that after enjoying the blessings, you must not forget the LORD who delivered you from bondage in Egypt, highlighting the importance of remembrance and gratitude.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 6:13, what three actions must you do in relation to the LORD your God?
options: Fear Him, serve Him, and swear by His name
Build altars, sacrifice animals, and pray
Ignore other gods, worship idols, and fast
Celebrate festivals, give gifts, and sing hymns
questions.correctAnswer: Fear Him, serve Him, and swear by His name
questions.explanation: Verse 13 commands fearing the LORD, serving Him, and swearing by His name as expressions of reverence and covenant loyalty.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 6:14 forbid the Israelites from doing?
options: Going after other gods of the surrounding peoples
questions.correctAnswer: Going after other gods of the surrounding peoples
questions.explanation: Verse 14 instructs the Israelites not to follow other gods of the nations around them, emphasizing exclusive devotion to the LORD.

questions.question: Why does the LORD describe Himself as a jealous God in Deuteronomy 6:15?
options: Because He desires exclusive worship and will punish idolatry
Because He wants the Israelites to build many altars
Because He enjoys festivals and sacrifices
Because He is angry with all nations
questions.correctAnswer: Because He desires exclusive worship and will punish idolatry
questions.explanation: Verse 15 explains that the LORD is a jealous God to warn against idolatry, lest His anger be kindled and destroy the people.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 6:16, what are the Israelites commanded not to do to the LORD their God?
options: Tempt Him as they did at Massah
questions.correctAnswer: Tempt Him as they did at Massah
questions.explanation: Verse 16 forbids tempting God as the Israelites did previously in Massah, referring to testing God’s patience and faithfulness.

questions.question: What is the main duty described in Deuteronomy 6:17 that the Israelites must perform?
options: Diligently keep the commandments, testimonies, and statutes of the LORD
Build a temple in every city
Gather at the mountain every Sabbath
questions.correctAnswer: Diligently keep the commandments, testimonies, and statutes of the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 17 highlights the necessity of diligently obeying all the LORD’s commands and laws as the foundation of covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What will happen if the Israelites do what is right and good in the sight of the LORD according to Deuteronomy 6:18?
options: It will be well with them and they will possess the good land
They will become rulers over other nations
They will be given wealth and fame
questions.correctAnswer: It will be well with them and they will possess the good land
questions.explanation: Verse 18 promises wellbeing and possession of the promised land if the Israelites do what is right and good in the LORD’s sight, linking obedience to blessing.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 6:15 warn will happen if the Israelites follow other gods?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 15 warns that the LORD’s anger will be kindled and He may destroy the Israelites from the face of the earth if they follow other gods, showing the seriousness of idolatry.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 6:12, the Israelites should remember the LORD who brought them out of Egypt to prevent forgetting Him after enjoying blessings.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 12 explicitly instructs the Israelites to beware lest they forget the LORD who delivered them from Egypt, especially after they have eaten and are full in the promised land.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 6:16, it is acceptable to test the LORD your God if you are unsure of His power.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 16 clearly commands not to tempt the LORD your God as the Israelites did at Massah, indicating that testing God is forbidden.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 6:12 relate to verses 10 and 11 concerning the blessings in the promised land?
options: It warns not to forget the LORD after enjoying the blessings described in verses 10 and 11
It commands to build altars on the goodly cities
It instructs to share the blessings with surrounding nations
It advises to return to Egypt if the land is not fruitful
questions.correctAnswer: It warns not to forget the LORD after enjoying the blessings described in verses 10 and 11
questions.explanation: Verse 12 acts as a caution to remember God after receiving the blessings of cities, houses, wells, vineyards, and olive trees described in verses 10 and 11, emphasizing gratitude and faithfulness.

questions.question: What blessing does Deuteronomy 6:18 say will result from doing what is right and good in the LORD's sight, in connection with verse 17's command to keep God's statutes?
options: It will be well with you and you will possess the good land
You will be wealthy beyond measure
You will become a great nation
questions.correctAnswer: It will be well with you and you will possess the good land
questions.explanation: Verse 18 shows that obedience to the commandments (verse 17) leads to wellbeing and possession of the land promised to the fathers, linking faithful obedience to tangible blessings.

questions.question: Based on Deuteronomy 6:13-15, how does the chapter teach about the virtue of exclusive devotion to God?
options: By commanding fear, service, swearing by God's name, and forbidding other gods because God is jealous
By encouraging worship of multiple gods for protection
By allowing worship of gods of neighboring peoples
By focusing only on sacrifices and offerings
questions.correctAnswer: By commanding fear, service, swearing by God's name, and forbidding other gods because God is jealous
questions.explanation: These verses emphasize fearing and serving only the LORD, swearing by His name, and rejecting other gods because the LORD is a jealous God who punishes idolatry, teaching exclusive devotion.

hard.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Deuteronomy Chapter 6.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 6:19, what is the purpose of possessing the good land?
options: To cast out all thine enemies from before thee
To build temples for other gods
questions.correctAnswer: To cast out all thine enemies from before thee
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:19 states the purpose is 'To cast out all thine enemies from before thee,' meaning possession of the land involves driving out adversaries.

questions.question: What question does the son ask in the future according to Deuteronomy 6:20?
options: What mean the testimonies, and the statutes, and the judgments?
How do we conquer new lands?
Who is the LORD our God?
questions.correctAnswer: What mean the testimonies, and the statutes, and the judgments?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:20 records the son's question about the meaning of the testimonies, statutes, and judgments given by God.

questions.question: In Deuteronomy 6:21, how does the father describe the Israelites’ past status in Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: Pharaoh's bondmen
questions.explanation: The father explains in Deuteronomy 6:21 that the Israelites were 'Pharaoh's bondmen' in Egypt before God delivered them.

questions.question: What did the LORD show upon Egypt, Pharaoh, and his household according to Deuteronomy 6:22?
options: Signs and wonders, great and sore
questions.correctAnswer: Signs and wonders, great and sore
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:22 states that the LORD showed 'signs and wonders, great and sore' upon Egypt and Pharaoh’s household to demonstrate His power.

questions.question: What was the purpose of bringing Israel out of Egypt as stated in Deuteronomy 6:23?
options: To give them the land which He swore unto their fathers
To punish them for their sins
To wander in the wilderness forever
questions.correctAnswer: To give them the land which He swore unto their fathers
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:23 explains God brought Israel out of Egypt to give them the promised land sworn to their fathers.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 6:24, why did the LORD command the Israelites to keep His statutes and fear Him?
options: For their good always, that He might preserve them alive
To make them rulers over other nations
questions.correctAnswer: For their good always, that He might preserve them alive
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:24 teaches that obedience and fearing God is commanded for the Israelites' continual good and preservation of life.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 6:25 say will be the righteousness of Israel if they observe all commandments?
options: It will bring wealth and fame
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be our righteousness
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:25 states that observing God's commandments faithfully is counted as righteousness for Israel.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of loving God with all your heart as commanded in Deuteronomy 6:5?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 22:37
questions.explanation: Matthew 22:37 quotes Deuteronomy 6:5, emphasizing loving God with all heart, soul, and mind, fulfilling this command in the New Testament.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Deuteronomy 6:4-5 where the unity of God and love to God are declared?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:4-5 forms an inclusio framing Israel’s faith by stating the LORD is one and commanding love to Him, enclosing the core belief and duty.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'echad' in Deuteronomy 6:4 primarily signify?
questions.correctAnswer: One, unified and singular
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'echad' in Deuteronomy 6:4 signifies singular unity, emphasizing that the LORD our God is one unified God.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 6:12, what are the Israelites warned not to forget?
options: The LORD who brought them out of Egypt, from the house of bondage
The cities built by their fathers
The laws of the surrounding nations
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD who brought them out of Egypt, from the house of bondage
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:12 warns Israel not to forget the LORD who delivered them from Egyptian bondage.

questions.question: Which New Testament verse echoes the command to teach God’s words diligently to children as in Deuteronomy 6:7?
questions.correctAnswer: Ephesians 6:4
questions.explanation: Ephesians 6:4 echoes Deuteronomy 6:7 by instructing fathers to bring up children in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 6:16 instructs Israel to test the LORD their God just as they did in Massah.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:16 specifically commands not to tempt or test the LORD as they did in Massah, making the statement false.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 6:14 warns Israel not to follow other gods because the LORD is a jealous God.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:14-15 warns Israel against following other gods because the LORD is jealous and anger would result if they did.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 6:8-9, how were the commandments to be kept before the Israelites?
options: Bound on the hand and forehead, written on doorposts and gates
questions.correctAnswer: Bound on the hand and forehead, written on doorposts and gates
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:8-9 commands Israelites to bind the words on their hand and forehead and write them on house posts and gates as continual reminders.

theological.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Deuteronomy Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of God's commandments as stated in Deuteronomy 6:1?
options: To teach the people so they may obey in the promised land
To provide a ritual system for worship
To distinguish Israel from other nations
questions.correctAnswer: To teach the people so they may obey in the promised land
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:1 states that the commandments, statutes, and judgments were commanded by the LORD to teach the people, so that they might do them in the land they are about to possess.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 6:2, what is the intended effect on the life of those who fear the LORD and keep His commandments?
options: They will be free from suffering
questions.correctAnswer: Their days may be prolonged
questions.explanation: Verse 2 teaches that fearing the LORD and keeping His commandments leads to a prolonged life, emphasizing the covenantal blessing linked to obedience.

questions.question: What fundamental truth about God is proclaimed in Deuteronomy 6:4?
options: The LORD our God is one LORD
God is a God of many gods
The LORD is far from the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD our God is one LORD
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:4 affirms the foundational monotheistic confession that the LORD our God is one LORD, emphasizing God's unity and singularity.

questions.question: Which commandment in Deuteronomy 6 instructs how one should love God?
options: With all your heart, soul, and might
questions.correctAnswer: With all your heart, soul, and might
questions.explanation: Verse 5 commands to love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, soul, and might, highlighting the total devotion expected toward God.

questions.question: What practice does Deuteronomy 6:7 emphasize for passing on God's commandments?
options: Teaching children diligently throughout daily life
Writing commandments on scrolls to be stored
Singing songs only on the Sabbath
questions.correctAnswer: Teaching children diligently throughout daily life
questions.explanation: Verse 7 instructs to teach the commandments diligently to children and to talk of them at all times—sitting, walking, lying down, and rising up—indicating constant instruction.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 6:8-9 suggest God's commandments should be visibly represented?
options: Bound as signs on the hand and forehead, and written on house posts and gates
Recited once a year during festivals
questions.correctAnswer: Bound as signs on the hand and forehead, and written on house posts and gates
questions.explanation: Verses 8 and 9 direct that God's commandments be bound as signs upon the hand and forehead and written on the doorposts and gates, symbolizing continual remembrance and public declaration.

questions.question: What warning does Deuteronomy 6:12 give regarding Israel's future prosperity?
options: Beware lest you forget the LORD who delivered you from Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: Beware lest you forget the LORD who delivered you from Egypt
questions.explanation: Verse 12 warns Israel to not forget the LORD who brought them out of Egypt, cautioning against the spiritual danger of prosperity leading to forgetfulness of God.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Deuteronomy 6:15 when God is described as a 'jealous God'?
questions.correctAnswer: God's zeal for exclusive worship
questions.explanation: Verse 15 highlights God's attribute of jealousy, meaning His zeal and desire for exclusive worship by His people, which reflects His covenantal faithfulness and holiness.

questions.question: What is the theological significance of Deuteronomy 6:16's command not to tempt the LORD, referencing Massah?
options: It warns against testing God's faithfulness as Israel did at Massah
It prohibits any form of sacrifice
It commands building altars at Massah
questions.correctAnswer: It warns against testing God's faithfulness as Israel did at Massah
questions.explanation: Verse 16 recalls Israel's prior testing of God at Massah, teaching the doctrine that God's faithfulness should not be tested or put to proof presumptuously.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do Deuteronomy 6:17 and 6:18 convey about obedience?
options: Diligent obedience to God's commandments results in well-being and possession of the promised land
Obedience guarantees freedom from all trials
Only ritual acts are necessary for righteousness
Obedience is optional for God's favor
questions.correctAnswer: Diligent obedience to God's commandments results in well-being and possession of the promised land
questions.explanation: Verses 17 and 18 teach that diligently keeping God's commandments and doing what is right in His sight leads to well-being and inheriting the good land God promised, linking obedience to covenant blessing.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 6:20-23 connect Israel's history to their covenantal identity?
options: It instructs parents to teach children about deliverance from Egypt as a foundation of their faith
It commands building monuments to Pharaoh
It focuses on military conquest tactics
questions.correctAnswer: It instructs parents to teach children about deliverance from Egypt as a foundation of their faith
questions.explanation: Verses 20-23 establish that recalling God's mighty deliverance from Egypt and the giving of the land is central to Israel's identity and continual obedience to God's statutes.

questions.question: What doctrine is taught in Deuteronomy 6:24-25 regarding righteousness?
options: Obedience to God's commandments is considered righteousness
Righteousness is unrelated to the law
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God's commandments is considered righteousness
questions.explanation: Verses 24-25 teach that observing God's commandments as He has commanded is our righteousness, linking covenant obedience with righteousness before God.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is most clearly demonstrated by the promise of giving 'great and goodly cities' and 'houses full of all good things' as in Deuteronomy 6:10-11?
options: God's faithfulness to His covenant promises
questions.correctAnswer: God's faithfulness to His covenant promises
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 emphasize God's faithfulness in fulfilling His promises to the patriarchs by providing abundant blessings in the promised land.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that following Old Testament laws is obsolete for believers today. What does Deuteronomy 6:1-3 actually teach about the purpose of God's commandments?
options: God's commandments are given to instruct and bless His people, ensuring their well-being in the promised land
The laws were only for ancient Israel with no lasting value
The commandments were symbolic and not meant to be obeyed
The laws were temporary and replaced by other gods
questions.correctAnswer: God's commandments are given to instruct and bless His people, ensuring their well-being in the promised land
questions.explanation: Verses 1-3 show that God's commandments were intended to teach His people how to live rightly so that they might prosper and live long in the land He promised, demonstrating the enduring purpose of God's law for covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What synthesis of Deuteronomy 6:4-5 and 6:13 teaches about the nature of worship and service to God?
options: Worship and service to God must be exclusive, fearing Him and loving Him with all heart, soul, and might
Worship involves many gods and casual service
Service to God can be partial and indifferent
Love for God is unrelated to fear or service
questions.correctAnswer: Worship and service to God must be exclusive, fearing Him and loving Him with all heart, soul, and might
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:4-5 emphasizes loving God wholly, while 6:13 commands fearing and serving the LORD exclusively, together teaching that worship requires total devotion and exclusive allegiance.
